Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 46c6d45d7875a0328258a574e376ae75f7b2a64b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2015 23:35:25 +0300
Subject: [PATCH] cxlflash: off by one bug in cxlflash_show_port_status()

The > should be >= or we read one element past the end of the array.

Fixes: c21e0bbfc485 ('cxlflash: Base support for IBM CXL Flash Adapter')
Signed-off-by: Dan Carpenter <dan.carpenter@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Matthew R. Ochs <mrochs@linux.vnet.ibm.com>
Signed-off-by: James Bottomley <JBottomley@Odin.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c b/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
index 458ed838f83a..fde2ba9342dc 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c
@@ -586,7 +586,7 @@ static ssize_t cxlflash_show_port_status(struct device *dev,
 	u64 *fc_regs;
 
 	rc = kstrtouint((attr->attr.name + 4), 10, &port);
-	if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
+	if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
 		return 0;
 
 	fc_regs = &afu->afu_map->global.fc_regs[port][0];
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/scsi/cxlflash/main.c`**
- The condition in the `cxlflash_show_port_status` function was modified from `if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))` to `if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))`. This change ensures that the code does not read one element past the end of the array by allowing the `port` variable to be equal to `NUM_FC_PORTS`, which is the maximum valid index.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses an off-by-one bug that could lead to accessing an out-of-bounds element in the array. The change is directly related to the previous implementation that incorrectly allowed for an index greater than the maximum valid index, potentially causing undefined behavior or crashes. The patch is a fix for the bug introduced in a prior commit (`c21e0bbfc485`), which added base support for the IBM CXL Flash Adapter.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (rc || (port > NUM_FC_PORTS))
```
Reason:
The condition `port > NUM_FC_PORTS` allows the `port` index to equal `NUM_FC_PORTS`, which results in accessing an out-of-bounds element in the array `fc_regs`, leading to reading one element past the end of the array.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (rc || (port >= NUM_FC_PORTS))
```
Reason:
Changing the condition to `port >= NUM_FC_PORTS` ensures that the `port` index is always within valid bounds, preventing any out-of-bounds access when `port` is equal to `NUM_FC_PORTS`.
